key: Ask two questions in order: does the ulcer hurt, and what are the inguinal nodes doing? Painful ulcers are herpes with grouped vesicles and chancroid with a ragged ulcer and suppurating node; painless ulcers are syphilis with a clean chancre and rubbery nodes, LGV with a fleeting ulcer then buboes, and donovanosis with a beefy-red ulcer and no true nodes.
items: Painful grouped vesicles on a red base
hsv
Herpes simplex virus kills epithelial cells as it replicates, so clustered vesicles break into shallow ulcers that hurt.
Multinucleated giant cells on a Tzanck smear
hsv
Infected cells fuse into multinucleated giant cells. The smear cannot tell herpes simplex from varicella-zoster, so lesion PCR is the better test.
Latent virus in sacral ganglia that reactivates with stress
hsv
The virus travels up sensory nerves and stays latent in the sacral ganglia, so stress or illness can trigger recurrences at the same site.
Treated with acyclovir or valacyclovir
hsv
These drugs are activated by viral thymidine kinase and stop viral DNA polymerase. They shorten outbreaks but do not clear latent virus.
Deep ragged ulcer with a gray purulent base
chancroid
Haemophilus ducreyi causes a painful, ragged ulcer with a purulent base, unlike the clean-based syphilis chancre.
Gram-negative rods lined up like a school of fish
chancroid
H. ducreyi is a small gram-negative rod that lines up in chains in ulcer pus, the school-of-fish pattern.
Painful ulcer plus a tender unilateral node that may suppurate
chancroid
The painful ulcer separates this from LGV. The node on one side becomes tender and can drain through the skin.
Treated with azithromycin or ceftriaxone
chancroid
Azithromycin or ceftriaxone treats it. LGV and donovanosis need several weeks of treatment instead.
Single painless indurated ulcer with a clean base
syph
Treponema pallidum causes a firm, clean-based ulcer, and the lack of pain is why it is often missed.
Spirochetes seen on darkfield microscopy
syph
T. pallidum is too thin for a Gram stain, so chancre fluid is examined by darkfield microscopy, which can be positive before serology.
Rubbery, painless nodes on both sides
syph
Nearby nodes enlarge without acute inflammation, so they are firm and painless, unlike the painful buboes of chancroid and LGV.
Treated with benzathine penicillin G
syph
Long-acting penicillin treats syphilis because the spirochete stays penicillin sensitive. The first dose can cause a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction.
Small ulcer that heals before the nodes swell
lgv
Chlamydia L1 to L3 cause a tiny painless ulcer that heals within days, so patients come in weeks later because of the nodes.
Matted painful buboes with a groove sign
lgv
The L serovars spread through lymphatics to the groin nodes, which swell above and below the inguinal ligament and may drain through the skin.
Treated with doxycycline for several weeks
lgv
These invasive serovars need a much longer course than the 7 days that clears genital chlamydia.
Proctocolitis after rectal exposure
lgv
Rectal infection with L serovars causes bloody discharge, urgency and pain that can mimic inflammatory bowel disease.
Beefy-red ulcer that bleeds on contact
donov
Klebsiella granulomatis causes soft, friable tissue that bleeds easily. The ulcer is painless.
Donovan bodies in macrophages
donov
A Giemsa-stained smear or biopsy shows bacteria with a safety-pin look inside macrophages. These are Donovan bodies.
Subcutaneous swellings without true node enlargement
donov
Granulomatous inflammation makes swellings in the groin called pseudobuboes, not true enlarged lymph nodes.
Treated with azithromycin for several weeks
donov
Treatment continues until the ulcer has healed, which takes several weeks.
